items.title: Cavalcade of Stars
items.description: Jackie Gleason on segment of the popular 50's TV series "Cavalcade of Stars", doing a sketch called "The Honeymooners", which was later turned into a sitcom. "Cavalcade of Stars" started in 1949 and quickly became one of the most popular shows on The DuMont Television Network. Jackie Gleason was the 3rd and most popular host of the series. "The Honeymooners" started as a series of sketches, and later became a classic CBS sitcom still shown in syndication today. While the sitcom is still copyrighted, "Cavalcade of Stars" has long been public domain. This excerpt is all I have of the episode (I wish I could see the whole thing! Jackie did lots of different sketches back then). Rights: Public domain.

items.title: Fleischer Studios' Superman
items.description: The Fleischer Superman cartoons are a series of seventeen animated short films released in Technicolor by Paramount Pictures and based upon the comic book character Superman, making them his first animated appearance. They were originally produced by Fleischer Studios, which completed the initial short and eight further cartoons in 1941 and 1942. Production was resumed in May 1942 by Famous Studios, a successor company to Fleischer, which produced eight more cartoons in 1942 and 1943. Superman was the final animated series initiated by Fleischer Studios, before Famous Studios officially took over production. The first short, "Superman" (1941), alternatively known as "The Mad Scientist" would be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short of 1941. All the shorts fell into the public domain when DC Comics (then known as National Comics) failed to renew the copyrights for the shorts. List of shorts: Superman (1941) - alternatively known as "The Mad Scientist", Academy Award nominee for Best Animated Short of 1941 The Mechanical Monsters (1941) Billion Dollar Limited (1942) The Arctic Giant (1942) The Bulleteers (1942) The Magnetic Telescope (1942) Electric Earthquake (1942) Volcano (1942) Terror on the Midway (1942) Japoteurs (1942) Showdown (1942) Eleventh Hour (1942) Destruction, Inc. (1942) The Mummy Strikes (1943) Jungle Drums (1943) The Underground World (1943) Secret Agent (1943) The shorts were originally produced by Fleischer Studios and Famous Studios and were originally distributed by Paramount Pictures, but are all in the public domain, meaning that they are free to use and distribute. Creator: Fleischer Studios, Famous Studios, Paramount Pictures. Rights: Public domain.

items.title: Looney Tunes Classics: Collection
items.description: Explore a timeless collection of classic Looney Tunes cartoons, now available in the public domain. Relive the adventures of iconic characters like Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and Porky Pig in this handpicked selection of some of the best episodes from the golden age of animation. Enjoy the humor, creativity, and nostalgia of these beloved cartoons, suitable for all ages. Creator: Warner Bros.. Rights: Public domain.

items.title: Merri Melodies shorts
items.description: This collection compiles all Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies shorts that have entered the public domain, covering releases from 1929 through 1943 and totaling 439 minutes. The set includes original black‑and‑white cartoons as well as later unofficial colorized versions, and it carries content warnings for outdated racial stereotypes. Rights: Public domain.
